title: Regional GPU ops tacit brief — 2027-05-12
body:
Purpose:
Quick operational snapshot and action list for regional GPU health, capacity signals, and short-term mitigations. This is a working brief for on-call and capacity planning — not a finalized runbook.

High-level summary (last 7 days):
- Net available GPU capacity dipped ~9% Wed morning (5/10) due to a coordinated preemption event in ap-southeast and us-central spot pools. Latency SLOs were breached briefly for low-priority batches; user-facing requests stayed within 95th percentile target thanks to routing fallbacks.
- EMEA-west has steady headroom (estimated +16% reserve) through next week. APAC demand increasing ~22% week-over-week driven by a single enterprise customer ramp.
- Observability gap: we still lack per-model preemption counters in the region dashboards; current estimates rely on node-level eviction rates.

Telemetry highlights and weird signals:
- Preemption correlation: spot price spikes in provider B correlated with eviction clusters at 03:00–04:30 UTC on 5/10. Node churn pattern indicates >70% of evictions were from non-reserved nodes.
- Cold-start failures: small but actionable rate of KV-cache warmup timeouts on node restart (median warmup 11s vs expected 3s). This impacted low-latency routes for under-provisioned canaries.
- Autoscaler thrash: in us-central test pool, aggressive downscale policy removed nodes while jobs still in queue — increased queue latency for batch jobs by ~18%.

Region deep dives:
- APAC (ap-southeast):
  - Incident: preemption spike 05/10 03:10–04:00 UTC. Immediate mitigation: increase reserved (non-spot) fallback by +6 nodes for premium tenant routes; re-routed non-critical batch load to us-west for 90 min.
  - Short-term ask: sales/product to confirm whether the enterprise ramp should be considered long-lived. If yes, proposal to move 12 GPUs to Reserved pool by next billing cycle.
  - Action owner: Priya — prepare cost delta and billing impact by 5/18.

- US (us-central / us-west):
  - Observation: us-central experiencing spot volatility; us-west has stable node retention but higher average latency during peak hours (20:00–02:00 PDT).
  - Mitigation trial: throttled non-essential maintenance window (k8s upgrades) to off-peak and increased pre-warming windows for low-priority jobs by +5 minutes.
  - Action owner: Liam — run A/B for pre-warm window sizes (5m vs 10m) and report perf delta by 5/19.

- EMEA (eu-west, eu-north):
  - Good: steady supply, low eviction. Noted repeated small-scale restarts on a single AZ in eu-west — appears tied to a provider agent update. Scheduled to monitor with provider contact.
  - Action owner: Marta — vendor escalation ticket created (JIRA-9876). Follow up status 5/15.

Incidents & postmortem notes (short):
- 5/10 preemption event (ap-southeast + us-central) — root cause: provider spot-price surge + high proportion of overnight batch jobs scheduled without reservation.
  - What worked: smart routing to fallback-compatible model variants and burst into reserved pool for premium customers.
  - What failed: lack of per-model eviction metrics and slow KV-cache rebuilds.
  - Short fixes: temporary increase in reserved pool for premium routes; throttle batch job concurrency during preemption windows.
  - Longer-term items: add per-model eviction counters and KV-cache checkpointing to reduce warmup time.

Open action items (owners & due dates):
- Add per-model preemption metric to observability (MVP): Rashmi — due 2027-05-28.
- Cost impact calc for reserving 12 GPUs in ap-southeast (Priya) — due 2027-05-18.
- Pre-warm window A/B test (Liam) — start 5/15, report 5/19.
- Autoscaler policy review for test pools (Ethan) — update recommended thresholds by 5/20.
- KV-cache checkpoint prototype (engineering-ml): request spec submitted; follow-up meeting 5/17.

Short-term capacity ask for product/sales (for immediate planning):
- If enterprise customer in APAC confirms sustained usage, we should convert 12 GPUs to reserved (non-spot) for next month to avoid repeated preemption. Expect ~+$3.2k/month. Priya to confirm.

Runbook reminders / temporary playbook changes:
- During provider spot-price alerts (automated via slack webhook):
  - Step 1: triage on-call to confirm eviction cluster (on-call runbook link in slack).
  - Step 2: temporarily raise routing weight to reserved-capacity for premium routes (+10%) and throttle batch concurrency.
  - Step 3: if capacity < target after 10m, engage infra lead and consider cross-region re-route.
- Add this to on-call checklist after we ship per-model preemption metrics.

Meeting requests / syncs:
- Quick sync with product + AMs (internal) to confirm APAC account trajectory — target 5/14 EOD.
- Vendor check-in with provider contact about recurrent restarts in eu-west — 5/15.
- Capacity planning deep-dive (30m) for execs next week; proposed agenda: current headroom, cost to reserve, and impact on SLOs. Tentative 5/20.

Notes to self / friction items:
- Observability: add a lightweight per-model counter first (can be a Prom counter on inference proxy) rather than full telemetry pipeline change.
- Consider a short-term policy: mark long-running nightly batch jobs with lower eviction tolerance so autoscaler is less likely to downscale their nodes.

Appendix (quick numbers snapshot) — estimates as of 2027-05-12:
- Global available GPUs (poolable): 1,420
- Reserved (non-spot): 520
- Spot/ephemeral: 900
- Estimated headroom next 7 days (global, conservative): ~8%
- APAC headroom: +1% (tight if enterprise ramps continue)
- EMEA headroom: +16%

If anything above is unclear or someone wants to be removed/added from the follow-up list, ping me (Ethan).

Quick log of standup snippets (raw):
- 2027-05-12 09:05 — Priya: "apac spike — raised ticket; product alerted"
- 2027-05-12 09:12 — Marta: "eu-west AZ restarts — vendor investigating"
- 2027-05-12 09:30 — Liam: "starting pre-warm A/B design; need small infra sandbox"
- 2027-05-12 09:45 — Rashmi: "observability spec in progress; prototyping prom counter"

End of brief.
